applicant_utility.summary: This is AIMS South Africa's fully funded Structured Master's in Mathematical Science, and the round opening now is the January 2027 intake run specifically for South African applicants through the Mathematical Sciences stream portal. The published package covers tuition and research fees, on-site accommodation, three meals a day, medical insurance, flights to and from South Africa plus airport transfers, and a R2,200 per month stipend paid into a South African bank account. AIMS does not publish a closing day, so treat the end of October as the working deadline and submit well before the window closes, because shortlisting and an online interview still have to happen before final selection.
applicant_utility.best_fit: South African graduates with a four-year degree or a three-year degree plus an honours year, strong mathematical and computational training, and no previous AIMS scholarship.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your four-year degree, or three-year degree plus honours year, will be completed by December, the published cut-off for the January intake.
Register on the Mathematical Sciences stream portal at apply.aims.ac.za; do not use the AI for Science portal, which has no January intake.
Collect undergraduate and any postgraduate transcripts before starting the form, since both are requested uploads.
Prepare a CV, a cover letter and a representative sample of mathematical work in advance, as these are uploaded with the application.
Have a South African bank account ready: the stipend is paid directly into one and AIMS settles all other expenses itself.
Check you have never previously held a scholarship to study at an AIMS centre, as this is an explicit bar.
common_rejection_risks: Applying with a degree that will not be completed by December, the published cut-off for the January intake.
Applying through the AI for Science portal or for the September intake, neither of which is the January round for South African applicants.
Holding a previous AIMS scholarship, which makes an applicant ineligible regardless of merit.
Failing the residency and citizenship screen: you must be an African citizen and resident in Africa when you apply, with war-displaced applicants the only exception.
Leaving uploads incomplete, such as missing postgraduate transcripts, cover letter or sample work, which stalls the application before shortlisting.
Applying for the January intake as a non-South African, since AIMS publishes this intake specifically for South African applicants.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: AIMS covers tuition and research fees, accommodation, meals, medical insurance, flights and transfers, and pays the R2,200 monthly stipend, so the main out-of-pocket items are personal spending such as clothing, leisure and individual local travel in Cape Town, plus anything needed before arrival that falls outside the airport-transfer service; AIMS publishes no figure for these.
document_audit: The form asks for undergraduate AND postgraduate transcripts; applicants with no postgraduate study still need to handle those upload fields rather than leave them silently blank.
The cover letter and CV are separate uploads; combine them only if the portal explicitly allows it.
Sample work should be a representative, self-contained mathematical or computational piece.
Final-year students will only have current-year transcripts at application time, so make sure these are up to date before submitting.
alerts: The January 2027 window (August to October 2026) is closing this month and no day-level date is published, so assume the strictest reading and submit early.
Scholarship funds are managed by AIMS and not paid into your bank account; only the stipend reaches you, and it must be a South African account.
The Africa-wide September intake is a different round with its own January-to-March window; do not confuse the two when planning.
The AI for Science stream has no January intake, so its portal and deadlines do not apply to this scholarship.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on apply.aims.ac.za, complete the online application form, upload transcripts, CV, cover letter and sample work, then submit; shortlisted candidates are invited to an online interview before final selections are made.
